CORRECTED 2026-09-04 (phase-417 W-M2): verdicted `gap` -- "we should have it, nobody did it" -- while the shim REFUSES it loudly (`packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/qos.hpp:767` (in `rclcpp_compat.hpp` until phase-417 stage 6 step A deleted it), `NROS_RCLCPP_REFUSE_SYSTEM_DEFAULTS_QOS`). The ledger and the shipped code disagreed, and the code is right: upstream's `rmw_qos_profile_system_default` is ALL-SENTINEL -- every field says "let the RMW decide" -- and issue 0829 measured that resolving to depth 1 on Cyclone and 42 on zenoh. No concrete value can be correct, and `nros::QoS` has no sentinel by design, so a value here would be a confident wrong answer rather than a missing one. That is a decline, not a gap.

It was also the THIRD live inversion stage 3 found: the shim previously returned `QoS(10)`, which is `rmw_qos_profile_DEFAULT` -- a different upstream profile altogether.

Rust has `QoSProfile::system_default()`; C++ and C have no such preset. OUR LANGUAGES DISAGREE: our C++ ships exactly THREE QoS presets -- `QoS::default_profile()`, `QoS::sensor_data()`, `QoS::services()` (qos.hpp) -- and C ships the same three as constants (`RCLC_QOS_DEFAULT`, `RCLC_QOS_SENSOR_DATA`, `RCLC_QOS_SERVICES`), while Rust's `QoSProfile` ships twelve: topics, sensor_data, services, parameters, parameter_events, clock, action_status, system, px4, plus the BEST_EFFORT/RELIABLE consts. So the profiles our OWN Rust parameter, clock and action code publishes on are unspellable from C and C++, and a ported node has to open a DDS reference and retype the numbers. Not a divergence -- nothing about a device stops a `constexpr QoS` named constructor from existing; the presets are just values. Phase 379 W3. Note the semantics do not carry over intact: `rmw_qos_profile_system_default` means "leave every policy for the middleware to decide", and there is no middleware here to defer to -- the backend is linked at build time and the profile is fixed at compile time (RFC-0036). Our `system_default` is a concrete RELIABLE + VOLATILE + KEEP_LAST(1) value, and our policy enums carry no `SystemDefault` or `Unknown` discriminant on purpose.

phase-428 Q1 (2026-09-06): SITE. `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/qos.hpp:764-768` -- `class SystemDefaultsQoS : public QoS` whose only constructor is `template <typename T = void> SystemDefaultsQoS()` with `static_assert(detail::refuse<T>::value, NROS_RCLCPP_REFUSE_SYSTEM_DEFAULTS_QOS)` at `:767`; the message is `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/logging.hpp:225`.
